mathematical_findings.finding: Local MemLp 2 for both functionals gives an integrable product of their norms by Holder. A bounded transform yields Integrable and an absolute integral bound before any finite or infinite spectral summation. The cumulative bounds alone are not treated as integrability evidence.

The closed low cut and lower-open upper-closed geometric shells partition each next cut without endpoint loss. Finite cutoff bounds use geometric totals 2 and 4/3. Monotone nonnegative ENNReal integration establishes finite global norm integral and then global Integrable; only afterwards are the Bochner cutoff integrals shown to converge. Constant 516 is retained.

The carrier is the actual Gamma0(z) cusp-orbit type with its finite instance for nonzero level, crossed with all real heights. Its measure is counting measure times dt/cosh(pi*t). The exact restricted quadratic form is the sum over every cusp and the symmetric interval [-T,T]. For trivial character all cusps are singular; no selected finite proxy cusp family is substituted.

The Gamma0 matrix sends infinity to 1/z, and the printed arithmetic density gcd(w,z/w)/z evaluates to 1/z at w=1 and w=z. sqrt(n)*rho supplies the exact sqrt(m*n) factor. The defined continuous expression retains 1/(4*pi) outside the height measure. These algebraic facts are not an automorphic Fourier normalization or an equality with the physical Kloosterman source.

The literal integrand is H*conj(M(-k))*N(k). The previously proved common-weight identity at -k restores the original +k m-phase when conjugated. The n coefficient retains beta(nu*n,z), its coprime gate, the original signed cusp phase and k2/k3 phases. beta need not be real and is not conjugated. The same P.negativeCusp flag selects rhoOne at +n or -n.

The cusp level is explicitly tied by z=(P.packet r).level. The scale is the existing P.Y0. For every real T>=1 the two cumulative hypotheses use density 1/z and lengths P.V and P.U/nu, with constants fixed before T. Existing literal identities give C1*card(mCarrier) and C2*originalNEnergy, preserving arbitrary complex beta. The theorem is fixed in P,k,r,z; it does not supply constants uniform in level/residue/nu or positive-frequency/dyadic-support hypotheses.
